subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Wirecard's Phantom Billions
description: A quick win: understand Wirecard's Phantom Billions.

hook.text: Wirecard reported €1.9 billion in cash that didn't exist. The money was never in the bank accounts.

buildup.text: Germany's fintech darling claimed massive profits from Asian payment processing. Auditors accepted the claims.

discovery.text: FT journalist Dan McCrum investigated for years. Wirecard sued him and called the allegations racist.

twist.text: German regulators investigated McCrum instead of Wirecard, even banning short-selling of Wirecard stock.

climax.text: When EY finally checked the bank accounts, €1.9 billion was simply missing. The CEO was arrested.

punchline.text: €1.9 billion missing. Regulators protected the fraudsters.

quiz.question: What did German regulators do when Wirecard fraud was alleged?
options: Investigated the journalist instead of the company
